title: With some surviving, some others stumbling on steps,

blocks.text: With some surviving, some others stumbling on steps, the Singhs tried to push along the narrow mountain route while the river drowned those who tumbled from the slopes below. The passage became so choked with desperate fighters that neither the men behind could reach the front nor those ahead could turn back in any orderly way.

Everywhere the retreat turned into a siege, because there was no room to march forward and no path to reverse the movement. Men slipped, collided, and were swept away, while the crush of bodies on the hill made every small mistake fatal.

Hunger and thirst then deepened the ordeal until it seemed impossible even to drink a drop of water. As the pressure mounted, the Mughal side hardened the pursuit further by placing a reward of five rupees for each Sikh’s head, turning the retreat into a hunted massacre.
